stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.def-1.1.title: Stability condition on a triangulated category (introduction form)
stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.def-1.1.informal: The paper's introductory definition: a central charge Z on K(D) together with full additive subcategories P(phi) of semistable objects of phase phi, satisfying the shift, Hom-vanishing and Harder-Narasimhan axioms.
stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.def-1.1.quote: Definition 1.1. stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.def-3.3.title: Slicing of a triangulated category
stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.def-3.3.informal: A slicing is the P-half of a stability condition on its own: full additive subcategories P(phi) closed under the shift axiom P(phi + 1) = P(phi)[1], Hom-vanishing for decreasing phases, and existence of Harder-Narasimhan filtrations.
stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.def-3.3.quote: Definition 3.3. stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.lem-3.4.title: Objects of a slicing over an interval of length at most one
stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.lem-3.4.informal: For an interval I of length at most one, the subcategory P(I) is quasi-abelian and its strict short exact sequences are exactly the distinguished triangles with all three vertices in P(I). This is the lemma the repo's interval-subcategory machinery rests on.
stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.lem-3.4.quote: Lemma 3.4. Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a slicing of a triangulated category $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$ and let $I\subset\mathbb{R}$ be an interval of length at most one. Suppose $\textstyle{A\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$$\textstyle{E\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$$\textstyle{B\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ is a triangle in $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$, all of whose vertices are nonzero objects of $\mathcal{P}(I)$. Then there are inequalities $\phi^{+}(A)\leqslant\phi^{+}(E)$ and $\phi^{-}(E)\leqslant\phi^{-}(B)$.

stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.def-5.1.title: Stability condition as a central charge plus a slicing
stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.def-5.1.informal: The form this repo formalizes against: a group homomorphism Z on K(D) together with a slicing P, compatible via Z(E) = m(E) exp(i pi phi) for nonzero E in P(phi).
stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.def-5.1.quote: Definition 5.1. A stability condition $\sigma=(Z,\mathcal{P})$ on a triangulated category $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$ consists of a group homomorphism $Z\colon{{K}}(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}})\to\mathbb{C}$ and a slicing $\mathcal{P}$ of $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$ such that if $0\neq E\in\mathcal{P}(\phi)$ then $Z(E)=m(E)\exp(i\pi\phi)$ for some $m(E)\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}$.

stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.def-5.7.title: Locally-finite slicing and locally-finite stability condition
stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.def-5.7.informal: A slicing is locally-finite when some eta > 0 makes every P((t - eta, t + eta)) of finite length. This is the axiom the repo transports along an autoequivalence, and the one whose eta survives unchanged under Aut but not under a phase relabelling.
stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.def-5.7.quote: Definition 5.7. A slicing $\mathcal{P}$ of a triangulated category $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$ is locally-finite if there exists a real number $\eta>0$ such that for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$ the quasi-abelian category $\mathcal{P}((t-\eta,t+\eta))\subset\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$ is of finite length. A stability condition $(Z,\mathcal{P})$ is locally-finite if the corresponding slicing $\mathcal{P}$ is.

stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.prop-8..title: The generalised metric on the space of stability conditions
stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.prop-8..informal: Stab(D) carries a generalised metric d built from the sup over nonzero objects of the phase and mass discrepancies between two stability conditions.
stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.prop-8..quote: Proposition 8.1. Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$ be a triangulated category. The function $d(\sigma_{1},\sigma_{2})=\sup_{0\neq E\in\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}\bigg{\{}|\phi^{-}_{\sigma_{2}}(E)-\phi^{-}_{\sigma_{1}}(E)|,|\phi^{+}_{\sigma_{2}}(E)-\phi^{+}_{\sigma_{1}}(E)|,|\log\frac{m_{\sigma_{2}}(E)}{m_{\sigma_{1}}(E)}|\bigg{\}}\in[0,\infty]$ defines a generalised metric on $\operatorname{Stab}(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}})$. The induced topology is the same as that defined in Section 6.

stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.lem-8.2.title: GL+(2,R)~ acts on the right of Stab(D); Aut(D) acts on the left
stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.lem-8.2.informal: THE statement this repo's lane 1 exists for. Stab(D) carries a right action of GL+(2,R)~ -- which the paper names as the universal covering space of GL+(2,R) -- and a left action by isometries of Aut(D), and the two actions commute.
stmt:a520a8d4f877:bridgeland2007.lem-8.2.quote: Lemma 8.2. The generalised metric space $\operatorname{Stab}(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}})$ carries a right action of the group ${\tilde{\operatorname{GL^{+}}}}(2,\mathbb{R})$, the universal covering space of $\operatorname{GL^{+}}(2,\mathbb{R})$, and a left action by isometries of the group $\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}})$ of exact autoequivalences of $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$. These two actions commute.

frontier.statement: GL+(2,R)~ is defined here as a group of compatible pairs, NOT as a universal covering space. The covering-space facts the paper's phrase asserts -- projection surjective, fibre Z, simple connectedness -- are absent from Mathlib at the pinned revision and unproved here. The NAME asserts more than the proved content.

stmt:a520a8d4f877:obl-gltilde-universal-.title: Establish GL+(2,R)~ as the universal cover of GL+(2,R)
stmt:a520a8d4f877:obl-gltilde-universal-.informal: Owed work, not a paper statement. Lemma 8.2 names GL+(2,R)~ as the universal covering space; this repo defines it as a group of compatible pairs and proves only that it is a group.
